current.notes: v6: one clarification, no behaviour change on the memory tools themselves. On an ok `claim` response, the `memory` section is OMITTED when no note concerns the claimed paths, rather than sent as an empty array. This follows contract "Brief on claim" v1 (claude-token-diet) and the compact-row rule of no empty arrays; earlier versions of this contract read as if `memory` were always present, and tests/memory_layer.rs now asserts absence rather than an empty array. When present it is still at most CLAIM_MEMORY_LIMIT (5) digests, never a body. Also confirmed landed since v5: both literal limit strings in src/server.rs now read default 10, max 50, matching the constants. Everything else in v5 stands.

history.notes: v2 CHANGES TWO THINGS for the store glue, see notice 6414b67e. (1) Permalink::file_name() is now Permalink::file_path(); (2) permalinks may contain / folder segments, so the memory directory scan must RECURSE and the writer must create parent directories. Reason: the repo's own Basic Memory notes in .memory/ use permalinks like `tirith/design/pre-alpha-build`, and a flat namespace broke the compatibility promise in ADR-0011. An integration test that parses the real .memory/ notes caught it and now guards it. Escaping the directory is impossible: `.` is outside the allowed charset, so `..` cannot be spelled; there is a unit test for that. STATUS: src/memory.rs, src/types.rs (MemoryId), src/lib.rs, tests/memory_layer.rs and the docs are DONE and green (31 unit + 8 integration + 4 doc tests, clippy pedantic clean, rustfmt clean). Still waiting on storage-claude's "incremental persistence landed" notice before adding glue to state.rs/store.rs/server.rs.

history.notes: v3 is the SHIPPED shape: the three tools are registered on the server and tested over a real daemon. Changes from v2, all in the tool responses: memory_search returns {count, truncated, notes[]} where each row is the note plus a `score` field, instead of results[{note, score}]; this matches the list convention storage-claude is standardising in tasks 89b35cb6/e3e652b1, so that work does not have to touch memory code. limit defaults to 20 and clamps to 100. memory_read takes depth 0..=3 and returns invalid above that. claim now carries `memory`, at most 5 notes, each {permalink, title, kind, paths, updated_at, excerpt}, never a body. All three tools go through the existing `finish` and the ok/not_found/invalid helpers, so task e3e652b1 stays a single-place change. Note for whoever standardises listing: memory_search results are ranked by score, NOT newest-first, so types::Page::newest_first cannot be used on them as it would re-sort and destroy the ranking; build Page{items, total} directly if you want uniform fields.

history.notes: v4, SHIPPED and tested over a real daemon. Four changes from v3, all driven by head-dev-fable's audit and benchmark. (1) Listings carry digests, never bodies: memory_search rows and memory_read's `related` rows are MemoryDigest {permalink, title, kind, paths, tags, updated_at, excerpt} plus `score` on search rows; only memory_read's `note` has a body. The claim brief's `memory` rows are the same type, so they now include `tags` (claude-token-diet: the claim section of 04-primitives.md says so). (2) memory_write takes `if_updated_at`; a stale value is status `conflict` with `permalink` and the real `updated_at`, the same status shape a refused claim uses. (3) New tool memory_delete {agent, name} returning ok {removed: digest} or not_found; the file is unlinked via Delta.memory_removed (persistence seam v3) and stays gone across restart. (4) Reads no longer hold the State lock while scoring: Inner holds Arc<MemoryBook>, reads take a pointer clone through `access` (leases still renew) and score after releasing; writes use Arc::make_mut. Public State signatures unchanged. Also: `related` is capped at MAX_RELATED (20) and comes from a reverse-relation index instead of a scan. Limits stay 20/100 (head-dev-fable confirmed; 10/50 was only for body-carrying rows). Schema budget: memory_write's description and if_updated_at doc were trimmed to keep every tool under 500 chars; tests/http_roundtrip.rs TOOL_LIST_LIMIT raised 6_656 -> 7_000 with a comment naming memory_delete and if_updated_at, per ADR-0017.

history.notes: v5: one change from v4. memory_search `limit` now defaults to 10 and clamps to 50 (was 20 and 100). Decided by head-dev-fable on token grounds once the latency argument was settled: ten digest rows are about 2.3 KB, which keeps a search response below a notice listing, as ADR-0013 wants; at 20 it was the largest response in the system at 4.7 KB. Behavior is live as soon as this lands because the constants DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT and MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT live in src/memory.rs and server.rs imports them. Two LITERAL strings in src/server.rs still say "default 20, max 100" and are wrong until claude-token-diet updates them in its current window, which I have asked for by message rather than reopening the file: the `limit` field doc on MemorySearchInput (line ~416) and the memory_search tool description (line ~1566). Everything else in v4 stands.
